hints.content:
The greatest common factor of $14x^2$ and $28x^5$ is $14x^2$.

[[☃ explanation 2]]

Now we need to factor $14x^2$ out of $14x^2 + 28x^5$.

options.explanation:
We find the prime factors of each term:

$\begin{align}
14x^2&=\blueD{(2)}\maroonD{(7)}\goldD{(x)(x)}
\\\\
28x^5&=\blueD{(2)}(2)\maroonD{(7)}\goldD{(x)(x)}(x)(x)(x)
\end{align}$

The greatest common factor is the product of all the shared parts:

$\blueD{(2)}\maroonD{(7)}\goldD{(x)(x)}=14x^2$
